review_notes: I read the whole file. It has two integrability and integral lemmas and one definition, `paperFullLowHeightContribution`. That definition is a project-specific tsum over levels of a supremum over nonzero `lam` of the norm of a finite height sum. It specialises the project's own Carleson-type objects (`disjointLevelAtomSum`, `dyadicPsi`, `phase`, `oscillatoryScaleIndex`), and Mathlib has no counterpart. The file proves it equal to the existing `paperFullLowContribution`. That equality is intentional and documented as a literal match to the paper's formula, so I did not treat it as an avoidable competing concept. The theorems are excluded from this rubric as standalone results. I did not search Mathlib for a matching concept. I found none, and the supplied files give no evidence of one.
